Question: My colleague thinks she is my boss but we are on the same management level. What can I say to her to put her in her place? She is rude, disrespectful, and arrogant.
Answer: It sounds like you have a grudge against your coworker, she is rude, disrespectful and arrogant, and you want to put her in her place. Why not take her out to lunch, and explain that you feel that she is acting like your boss, and see what she says. She might just have a dominant personality, and thinks her ways are more efficient. She might not even be aware that you don't like, what she might think are suggestions. There is no reason to put her in her place. Because in theory, you two are equals, friendly coworkers. How do you put someone in that place. No, what you want to do, is put her down, and make her feel bad. You want a chance to vent all the frustration that has been building inside of you. But do you want to make an enemy at work, that will try and destroy your career, or do you want your workplace to be a nice place to advance? Respectfully point out how you feel when she makes suggestions, and she will probably mellow right out.

Question: What single car epitomized everything wrong with the US auto industry in the 70s?
Answer: I'm going to say the Chevette, you take a name that is halfway between the nice Chevelle and the sporty Corvette, and people will buy it. It was the best selling car in North America in 1979. It had a top speed of 83 mph, and a zero to 60 time of 19 seconds. It was GMs first car to have a timing belt, instead of a chain. It was ugly, and tiny. Yet it was the best selling car in North America, what does that tell you about the cars in North America during the late 1970s? I think the fact that it was a step up from it's predecessor, the Vega, that fooled people.

Question: Do oil rig workers typically spend months at a time on the rig without coming on land?
Answer: 99 percent of oil rigs are on land. So I assume that you are talking about the relatively rare offshore oil rigs. Depending on the location and the company, they would typically do a rotation, anything between 2 weeks on and 2 weeks off, and two months on and two months off. It's highly unlikely that anyone will work longer than 2 months straight. There are a few oil rigs so close to and, that the crew will come home on a fast crewboat every night.

Name: Bob Wilson
Question: Why do people not tip their movers even if they think they are doing an excellent job? How does tipping work in the US, where it is expected in most places except for restaurants, bars, and cafes?
Answer: I don't tip the police officer for arresting someone, I don't tip the plumber that installed my plumbing when the house was built. Consequently, I don't tip him when he installs my new dishwasher, five years later. I don't tip my mail person who delivers my mail, but I do leave them a Christmas card, so I don't tip the person that I have paid to deliver my furniture. I don't tip the building inspector for passing my building. I don't tip the county clerk for issuing my building permit. I don't tip the cashier at the grocery store. So I don't tip the cashier at the fast food place. I always found it odd, growing up 55 years ago, that I never once received a tip for filling up a cars gas tank, in the pouring rain, or when it was 40 below, yet the waitress in the restaurant that was attached to our gas station, got tipped, and she was paid a higher wage than me, to work in better conditions. I can't explain tipping (bribing) , it is a mystery. You are supposed to tip in sit down restaurants, bars and taxis. But it then crept to pizza delivery, then to hotel maids, bell boys, etc. Now my local hardware prompts me for a tip ,when I pay for the nuts and bolts I picked up myself. Who gets that money. Now that tips are almost always paid by credit card, you know that the server that you are leaving the tip for isn't getting it all. Tipping is just another word for bribe. Wages need to be adjusted accordingly.

Question: Why are liberals lying about Clarence Thomas? He's broken no law. The Left claims he "broke a longstanding tradition" by accepting trips, but those were all personal and the invites came from someone who's been a best friend for decades.
Answer: Up here in Canada, one of our Prime Ministers first acts, was to remove the itemization of things on expense accounts for MPs, and increase the expense account by 20 percent. Then he took three vacations to the Aga Khans private Island resort, while deciding whether the Canadian government should give $55,000,000 to the Agha Khans foundation. He finally decided to give the money to the Aga Khan, after his third vacation.The estimated cost for Justin Trudeau and his friends and family to stay on the island, was $500,000. That doesn't include flying on the government jet to the island, or the cost of the security guards. But I does include the cost of the private helicopter that the Aga Khan supplied, to get him from the airport to the island. After an MP had been caught using someone's private helicopter a couple of decades ago, they passed a specific law against it. Trudeau claimed that he only used the helicopter, because there was no other way to get to the private island. But somehow, all of his staff got there, without one. Because expenses were no longer itemized, there was no way to track where he had been. But you can't keep something this big wrapped up, so someone leaked his third trip to the media. He had not reported the trips obviously. There was an investigation, the Ethics commissioner found him guilty, but has no authority to impose a penalty. In this case the Prime Minister was accepting vacations worth $500,000 from a registered lobbyist, while deciding whether or not to give the lobbyist $55,000,000. His supporters elected him twice since then. You can't make this stuff up. I'm a Canadian and not directly affected by Clarence Thomas, but it looks bad. That's a lot of money, even spread out over twenty years. There are two things that make it less serious than Trudeaus faux pas, one, he never tried a case that involved the donor, and two, he was friends with the donor. I figure that if the left in Canada voted for Trudeau after this, that the left in the US, shouldn't be too upset about Thomas.
